title: Hydraulic Control Valve Assembly
model_title: Hydraulic Control Valve Assembly (Manifold with Directional, Pressure & Flow Valves)

introduction.definition: A hydraulic control valve assembly mounts several valves on a manifold block. Drilled galleries carry the pump pressure (P) and the tank return (T) to each valve station. Directional valves route oil to the actuator work ports (A and B); a relief valve limits pressure; flow-control valves set actuator speed. Mounting valves on a manifold saves piping and leak points.
key_points: P = pressure, T = tank, A/B = work ports
Spool position decides the flow path
introduction.summary: A hydraulic control valve assembly mounts several valves on one manifold block. Directional valves route oil to the actuators (P→A, B→T or P→B, A→T), a relief valve limits pressure and a flow control sets actuator speed — compact, with fewer leak points than piped valves.

foundation: Mount on a level, rigid base with access for filters, gauges and fill; drip tray/bund under the reservoir.
alignment: Align motor and pump with the bell housing and coupling; mount cylinders so the rod is not side-loaded (use spherical bearings/clevises).
piping: Clean (pickled/flushed) pipework sized for velocity (typical guide: suction ≲ 1.2 m/s, pressure 3–6 m/s, return ≲ 3 m/s); hoses not twisted or rubbing; correct fittings for pressure.
Fit pressure gauges/test points, and relief protection on every pressure source.
commissioning: Fill through a filter with the specified oil; flush the system to the target cleanliness (ISO 4406 code).
Bleed air; start with relief valves backed off, then set pressures; check for leaks, temperatures and noise.

routine.task: Check for external leaks and solenoid temperatures.

periodic.task: Check relief setting with a test gauge.

overhaul.task: Replace seals and solenoid coils; clean spools.

lubrication: No lubrication — oil cleanliness is key.

symptoms: Actuator does not move or moves slowly

safety: Lock out and depressurise before removing valves; manual overrides can move actuators unexpectedly.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Hydraulic Control Valve Assembly.
Check for external leaks and solenoid temperatures.
Check relief setting with a test gauge.
Replace seals and solenoid coils; clean spools.
Watch for spool sticking: actuator does not move or moves slowly. Common cause: contamination (silting), varnish.
Watch for relief valve chattering: noise, pressure oscillation. Common cause: wrong setting, worn seat.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
